title: Editor save and binary export silently drop nodes inside an instanced subscene (missing `[editable]` tag)
body:
### Tested versions

Reproduced: `4.7.2-stable`, `4.8.dev4.official.b56a91878`

### System information

Windows 10 (build 19045)

### Issue description

A scene file that contains nodes placed **inside an instanced subscene** (under the subscene's internal nodes — not as direct children of the instance root) and **without** an `[editable path="..."]` entry:

- **loads and runs perfectly** (F5, runtime instantiation): the nodes exist and work;
- **silently loses those nodes** when:
  - saving the scene in the editor (Ctrl+S) — the nodes are visible and editable in the Scene dock, but are removed from the saved `.tscn` without any warning;
  - exporting with *Convert Text Resources To Binary on export* enabled (the conversion repacks every scene through `PackedScene::pack()`).

Direct children of the instance root are **not** affected — only nodes whose parent path traverses the subscene's internal nodes. In the attached MRP, `ShallowLabel` survives while `InsideLabel` is dropped in the same scene, which makes the failure boundary quite confusing.

The `PackedScene.pack()` documentation states: *"Packs the path node, and all owned sub-nodes, into this PackedScene."* The dropped nodes have `owner` set correctly, so the documented contract is silently violated: `pack()` returns `OK`, no warning is printed anywhere, and the loss only surfaces later (in our case — as an empty screen in the exported build).

The editor UI cannot produce such files (adding nodes under an instance requires enabling *Editable Children*, which writes the `[editable]` tag), which likely explains why this file-format facet hasn't been reported before. Such files do occur in practice via hand-editing of `.tscn`, VCS merges (a conflict can keep the node lines but drop the `[editable]` line), and third-party tooling. The runtime facet of the same guard is reported in #90823.

- **loads and runs perfectly** (F5, runtime instantiation): the nodes exist and work;
- **silently loses those nodes** when:
  - saving the scene in the editor (Ctrl+S) — the nodes are visible and editable in the Scene dock, but are removed from the saved `.tscn` without any warning;
  - exporting with *Convert Text Resources To Binary on export* enabled (the conversion repacks every scene through `PackedScene::pack()`).

Direct children of the instance root are **not** affected — only nodes whose parent path traverses the subscene's internal nodes. In the attached MRP, `ShallowLabel` survives while `InsideLabel` is dropped in the same scene, which makes the failure boundary quite confusing.

The `PackedScene.pack()` documentation states: *"Packs the path node, and all owned sub-nodes, into this PackedScene."* The dropped nodes have `owner` set correctly, so the documented contract is silently violated: `pack()` returns `OK`, no warning is printed anywhere, and the loss only surfaces later (in our case — as an empty screen in the exported build).

The editor UI cannot produce such files (adding nodes under an instance requires enabling *Editable Children*, which writes the `[editable]` tag), which likely explains why this file-format facet hasn't been reported before. Such files do occur in practice via hand-editing of `.tscn`, VCS merges (a conflict can keep the node lines but drop the `[editable]` line), and third-party tooling. The runtime facet of the same guard is reported in #90823.

The cause is in `SceneState::_parse_node` (scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp), which prunes the traversal at the first node that is not owned by the packed scene:

```cpp
//discard nodes that do not belong to be processed
if (p_node != p_owner && p_node->get_owner() != p_owner && !p_owner->is_editable_instance(p_node->get_owner())) {
    return OK; // also skips owned override nodes deeper in the subtree
}
```

The instanced subscene's internal nodes are owned by the subscene, so the whole branch is skipped — including override nodes that **are** owned by the packed scene root and sit deeper in that branch. The text resource loader has no such gate: it creates every node listed in the file, which is why loading and running works and the loss only appears on a save/export round-trip.

As for the expected behavior: at minimum a warning (on loading a scene that contains nodes under a non-editable instance, or when `pack()` is about to drop owned nodes) would already help; ideally the round-trip should be lossless — the pruning should skip the foreign nodes' data, not the whole branch.

Related: #90823 (runtime `pack()` facet of the same guard), #45886 (similar report from 3.x era).

### Steps to reproduce

Using the attached MRP (2 tiny scenes + a script):

1. Run the project — both labels are found:
   `RESULT inside_found=true direct_found=true`
2. Export a PCK with binary conversion on, run it — the label under the instance internals is silently gone:
   `RESULT inside_found=false direct_found=true`
3. Open `main.tscn` in the editor: both labels are visible in the Scene dock. Press Ctrl+S and reload the scene — `InsideLabel` has been removed from the file, without any warning.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp_pack_drops_nodes.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31823272/mrp_pack_drops_nodes.zip)
